To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Deep networks can be used to approximate any smooth function on a compact set to arbitrary accuracy; 2) The depth of the network is the only parameter that matters; and 3) The number of nodes in the hidden layers does not affect the approximation ability.

(1) deep neural networks can approximate functions with arbitrary accuracy, (2) deep neural networks with ReLU activation functions can approximate any function on the unit cube with a bounded derivative, and (3) deep neural networks cannot approximate any function on an arbitrary compact set in R d.

1) Deep Neural Networks can be exponentially more efficient than shallow networks, 2) The efficiency gain can be achieved even with the same number of parameters in the networks, 3) The efficiency gain is achieved by the depth of the network, and 4) The depth is the key to achieving efficiency gain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether deep neural networks (DNNs) can approximate any continuous functions on a compact set.
the expressive power of neural networks, and the question of how to construct neural networks with the right expressive power for the problem at hand.
understanding how deep neural networks work, and how to design new neural networks with better expressiveness and performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expressive power of a neural network is not a function of depth, but of the number of neurons in the network and the non-linearity of the network.
, in terms of the expressive power, deep neural networks are as powerful as the classical feed-forward networks.
, the expressive power of a deep neural network depends on the number of hidden layers, number of nodes in each layer and the activation functions used.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep neural networks can approximate any function with a finite number of discontinuities, but they are not able to express any function that is continuous but not smooth.
the expressive power of a deep neural network is not a function of depth alone, and that depth is not the only factor that affects the expressive power of neural networks.
deep neural networks with a fixed number of parameters can express any continuous function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep neural networks are capable of representing functions that are not representable by any shallow networks.
deep neural networks are not universal approximators in the sense that they can only approximate functions that are continuous.

, for a given network architecture, the expressive power of the network depends on both the depth and the width, and that the depth and width are coupled in the sense that increasing the depth can compensate for a decrease in the width, and vice versa.
